chunks: Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from his two brothers Ali and Dawud from Hammad from Abd al-Rahman ibn A'yan said:

We performed Hajj in one year and with us were children, so the sacrificial animals became scarce, so we acquired one sheep after another, so we sacrificed for ourselves and left our children [without sacrifice]. He said: Bukayr came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him, so he said: 'It was appropriate that you sacrifice for the children and you fast for yourselves. Since you did not do so, let the guardian of each child among you fast on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a child if their guardian did not sacrifice an animal for them during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the expiation (*kaffarah*) for omitting the sacrificial animal (*hady*) for young children accompanying their guardians during Hajj. The ruling establishes that the guardian bears the responsibility to fast for each child, reflecting the principle that the *wali* (guardian) acts as the proxy for the child's ritual obligations when the child is too young to perform them independently. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view on the transferability of ritual duties from dependents to their legal guardians in cases of necessity or omission.
